summary: Wrote Labs 1, 2 and 3 of Module 02 in src/en/module_02/20-labs-a.md. Lab 1 (backprop in NumPy, 7 steps, 7 code blocks, 2 plots) runs in about 9 s; Lab 2 (scalar autodiff engine, 8 steps, 8 blocks, 1 plot) in about 20 s; Lab 3 (optimisers, schedules, range test, 7 steps, 9 blocks, 3 plots) in about 7 s. All outputs were written by labrun --update and a final rerun reports ALL LABS MATCH for each. check.mjs reports 0 errors.
changes: Lab 1 matches the plan numbers (2.0e-7 kink, 0.327 initial loss, 2.81e-4 final MSE, 0.403 extrapolation MSE, 26x init gap).

Lab 2: PyTorch cross-check loss is 0.0347593932 (not the plan 0.0295951652), because the loop compares at step 100 after 100 updates (plan loss was after one more update). Engine-vs-PyTorch ratio is printed to the nearest power of ten (1,000, plan said about 700) so the output is stable; test accuracy 0.992.

Lab 3 differs from the plan: SGD+momentum range test steepest 0.048, min 0.310 at 0.44, stop 0.58 (step 159); Adam steepest 0.0024, min 0.249 at 0.017, stop 0.089 (step 132), so ratios are 20x/26x/6.5x not 13-25x. Shoot-out: momentum reaches loss 0.1 at epoch 4 (plan 3); validation accuracies 93.3 (SGD 0.05), 97.5, 97.2, 97.5, 96.7, 96.7; Nesterov and momentum are both near SGD 0.5. Schedules: constant ends 25.7% above the noise floor (plan 17%), step 0.2%, cosine 0.4%. Adam first step: 615 zero-gradient parameters (512 constant-pixel weights plus 103 second-layer weights), gradients 1.8e-7 to 6.4e-2, 0.9996 moved by more than 0.99 lr (plan 786, 1.1e-8..4.4e-2, 0.9988).
Prose was rewritten to the real outputs; the public text avoids mentioning the source tutorial.
issues: Some code lines exceed 88 characters (up to about 100) in a few blocks; not fixed.
Lab 1 step 2 text refers to Section 14 and Lab 3 refers to Lab 4, which are in other parts; the cross-references resolve in check.mjs.
Timing-dependent outputs are printed in coarse form so reruns match; Lab 2 engine seconds per step printed to one decimal could flip between 0.1 and 0.2 on a much faster or slower machine.
